pretreatments.description: Dewatering of sludge using a belt filter press to a water content of approximately 80%.
Dilution of dewatered sludge with deionized water to achieve a TS content of 15%.
Thermal treatment at temperatures between 50 °C and 80 °C for durations ranging from 15 to 90 min, using a controlled thermostatic water bath.
Rapid cooling of thermally treated sludge to 33 °C immediately after thermal treatment using cold water.
Measurement of sludge viscosity using a rate-controlled viscometer (Searle system) at various shear rates.
Batch anaerobic digestion experiments conducted in bottles with a 1:1 ratio of inoculum VS to substrate VS (R_I/S = 0.7) at mesophilic conditions (35 ± 2 °C, 60 times per minute shaking).
Semi-continuous HSAD experiments conducted in a pilot-scale digester with intermittent stirring (3 h stirring and 3 h off) at 35 ± 2 °C and varying SRTs (22 days and 15 days).
Monitoring of biogas production and digestion time during batch and semi-continuous anaerobic digestion experiments.
Measurement of physical and chemical parameters (TS, VS, COD, TAN, FAN, ALK, TP, C/N ratio) of the sludge and digestate.
Evaluation of the release of soluble organic substances (SCOD) and VFAs during thermal treatment.
